events.title: Authorization Code Flow | Spotify for Developers

events.fact: Spotify OAuth apps are created via the Spotify Developer Dashboard (developer.spotify.com/dashboard) by signing in with a Spotify account, entering an App Name and App Description, and agreeing to the Developer Terms of Service.
As of February 2026, development mode apps require a Spotify Premium account for the app owner and limit test users to 5 allowlisted accounts.

As of May 15, 2025, Spotify extended quota mode applications are restricted to organizations (established business entities), operating an active launched service with at least 250,000 monthly active users (MAUs), available in key Spotify markets, and applied for via a partner application form using a company email.

The official review timeline for quota extension / production access is up to six weeks, though community reports show waits ranging from 4 days to over 13 weeks during peak periods or upon resubmission.

Spotify provides OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code Flow, Client Credentials Flow, Authorization Code with PKCE (S256), and Device Code grant types. Access tokens expire in 3600 seconds (1 hour) and come with a refresh token.
The Composio redirect URI for Spotify is https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback
Spotify Web API rate limits are governed by how many requests an app makes per second, returning HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header when exceeded.

Spotify scopes range from read-only user data (user-read-private, user-read-email) to playback control (user-modify-playback-state) and playlist modification (playlist-modify-public), some of which require user consent.

events.message: Research done: 8 findings, 7 pages read, 3 probes.
Verdict drafted: Spotify requires an established business entity with 250k+ MAUs for production access, leaving public integrations gated behind stringent review criteria.
